name: Spirit v1.5 / v1.6
summary: Spirit AI's foundation model line is a straightforward VLA — current observation plus text instruction in, next action chunk out — that has competed unusually well on independent evaluation. Spirit v1.5 shipped with open weights on Hugging Face and took first place on the RoboChallenge Table30 physical-robot evaluation in January 2026. Spirit v1.6 then scored 1,924 on RoboArena, ahead of NVIDIA's Cosmos3-Nano-Policy at 1,881 and DreamZero at 1,763 — the first time a Chinese model led the benchmark NVIDIA co-developed with Stanford and Berkeley, and it happened two days after NVIDIA announced its own top placement. Reported strengths are flip-top articulated objects, delicate grasps and multi-step sequential tasks.
innovation: Demonstrates that a conventional action-chunking VLA, well executed, still competes with world-action models on real-robot Elo.
Open weights at v1.5 make a leaderboard-competitive policy reproducible.
matters: The benchmark that was supposed to settle vendor claims got its first upset, and it came from outside the US labs the map is otherwise dominated by.
limits: v1.6 itself is not open; only v1.5 weights are published.
No paper for either version, and the RoboArena margin over Cosmos3-Nano-Policy is within plausible Elo noise.
lineage: Standard action-chunked VLA practice, tuned hard against public real-robot evaluation.
